newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary will not soften economic policies - Horn.
newsitem.headline: Hungary will not soften economic policies - Horn.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Monday his government would not soften economic policies in 1997 to gain voters before general elections in 1998.
The latest opinion poll, published in December, showed the opposition party Young Democrats (Fidesz) and the senior governing coalition partner, the Socialists, leading with 16 percent each.
"We are not preparing for any measures aimed at improving the mood of the public artificially," Horn told a news conference.
Hungary has cut its soaring budget and current account deficits through a two-year-old strict austerity programme, which had led to a 15-percent slump in living standards.
Horn said the programme was successful and the government would not jeopardise the results by artificially raising living standards.
However, the fundamentals of sustainable economic growth have been created, and this was likely to help domestic consumption increase in 1997, Horn added.
Economic stability would remain a priority for the government in 1997, but further austerity measures were not necessary, he said.

The government in 1997 would concentrate on reforming health care and pension systems, improving public security, supporting small- and medium-size enterprises and establishing a national agricultural strategy, Horn said.
